quality_or_reveal_dependency: Selection does not depend on a product verdict or treatment advantage. Cause/alarm/correspondence and actual-only consensus seal before assignment reveal. Original records are never rewritten to repair publication.
retain: Frozen production tools, baseline/common revisions, independent designs and applicability, initial-author admission and exact initial/final production source capsules.
All public controller requests/events/results/submissions/selfclaims/source locks and positive resource closure, including failed requests and unaccepted final attempts.

All original private claims, failed acquisitions, licensed first-execution continuations, source/config/capture bindings, raw native observations, original PNGs, xcresult evidence, SDK logs and historical shared-workflow bytes.

All original independent cause and alarm outputs, original disagreements, supplemental judgments, correspondence, actual-only consensus, all15 anonymous packets, derivation ledgers and disclosure barriers.
Qualification observations, all rejected and corrected generic helper attempts, original failure records, frozen code/tests and bounded synthetic fixture preservation.

Timing and disk streams, their explicit measurement windows, failed work, clock corrections/discrepancies, publication/CI attempts and cleanup ownership records. Active streams use labeled immutable prefixes until their final closure.
excluded_regenerable_material: Apple/Android SDKs, simulator runtimes/device images, shared JDK/Gradle distributions and caches, signing material, Git object databases and complete upstream checkouts.
Owned DerivedData/.build/Gradle compiled dependency caches and SDK precompiled modules. Preserve their commands, exit status, logs, source/compiled-input proofs and exact source capsules instead.
Redundant packed/decoded/archive transport scratch after the externally pinned transport, byte verification and required virtual restore/replay pass.
raw_byte_rules: Original source, expected values, native facts, PNG bytes, statuses, array order, original absolute reference keys and recorded failures remain exact.
Every selected regular file is inventoried with original path, SHA256, byte length and mode. Archive shards remain below the fixed 95MiB compressed ceiling.

Symlinks/special/unsafe synthetic negative fixtures are preserved as explicit structural metadata and safe byte copies where applicable; targets are never followed or re-created as active external links.
Cold transport only compresses original archive metadata bytes. Independent stream verification and virtual restoration validate the original inner archive.
replay_before_cleanup: Verify each complete selected archive and all reconstructed original bytes against externally recorded pins.
Restore actual-study artifacts into a fresh read-only virtual namespace. Use the exact original-key Resolver without original-path fallback or JSON path rewriting.

Replay recorded public controller barriers and native acquisition/source/resource provenance; historical shared-workflow checks use the separately pinned HistoryReader, final delivery uses the final view.
Verify anonymous packet and cause/alarm/correspondence input/output seals, then reproduce fixed metric arithmetic from sealed correspondence, frozen applicability and audited timings.

State unsupported evaluator boundaries explicitly. Historical source-domain native/source-responsibility evaluator portability is unsupported and cannot be replaced by manufactured P; live frozen evaluation, provenance replay and generic current-host runtime qualification are separate claims.

cleanup.scope: Only positively owned closed generated cache and explicitly inventoried closed fixture/scratch roots; project source/docs/publications remain.
cleanup.preconditions: Record original root owner/marker, device/inode, exact target membership and byte inventory; verify archive/replay prerequisites; confirm no pending SDK process or acquired device remains.
cleanup.execution: Append cleanup intent, recheck each owned root and no-follow membership, remove only recorded owned targets, record retained/failing paths and measured logical/allocated bytes. No name-only global cleanup.
cleanup.protected: Shared SDK/JDK/Gradle caches, unrelated/user devices, main repository Git metadata and unrelated files are never targets.
cleanup.measurement: Keep the original disk meters running through archival and cleanup; close and retain their final streams/summaries, then preserve terminal publication/cleanup metadata separately. Group peaks are not summed.
